life_event: Mother dies of Carditas(inflammation of the heart, caused by infection)
Father Michael remarries
Father dies of tuberculosis
Hickey and his brother move to Lowell with their stepmother

Convicted of petit larceny Years later, Hickey confessed to psychiatrist Dr. James W. Putnam that right before his father died his older brother made a murderous attack on him. He would have been around 11 at that time. Expelled from Lowell High School during freshman year for the stealing
charges that occurred listed above. Date of first killing. Hickey contacted police and notified them that he had found coworker, Edwin W. Morey dead at the drugstore where he
worked. Cause of death is poison. Police have no suspicion that Hickey was involved in Morey’s death. Hired as Assistant Secretary for the YMCA; significant because having
this job put him near the type of victims he preferred; he was later fired from this job due to monetary improprieties
Hickey married Edith W. Lees
Son Harold P. Hickey born
Hickey and Edith divorce
Hickey murders Michael Kruck in Central Park Once in May and once in December, Hickey stayed at Keswick Colony, a
religious retreat in hopes to cure his alcoholism
Returned to Keswick Colony; stayed for 3 ½ months. Left April 1, 1912 In a drunken rage, Hickey was caught strangling a young boy in front of a
train; he was apprehended and soon questioned by police and charges were eventually dropped and was only fined for the assault Hickey murders Joey Joseph in Lackawanna and put his remains down a

latrine October Numerous postcards are sent to Chief Gilson and one to the father of Joey 11- 46 Joseph giving the police hints of where they could find the body and November describing the crime in detail 11, 1912
Hickey left again for Keswick Colony
Police show up to Keswick Colony and his interrogation begins
Hickey’s hearing begins.
Hickey is taken to jail. Hickey confesses to killing Joey Joseph and Michael Kruck and states
that he was successful in 3 killings and 12 attempts; Gets Life in Prison, after an unsuccessful attempt to plead not guilty by reason of insanity
Hickey dies
